וחכמים אומרים of the 33b.6-7 baraita (not the 33b.5 mishna's Chachamim)
מתני ליה רבי אלעזר לבריה (33b.8), the primary tradition
the ואמרי לה tradition naming R' Chiyya as the teacher
דתנן (33b.8-9): the barrel of teruma mishna
דתניא at 33b.21-34a.1: מום לא יהיה בו ... כל מום

anonymous redactorial voice of this sugya

props.gloss_en: R' Meir: one may let a congested firstborn's blood in a place where the cut makes no blemish
R' Meir: one may not let its blood in a place where the cut makes a blemish
Chachamim: one may let its blood even in a place where the cut makes a blemish
Chachamim: provided he does not slaughter it on account of that blemish
R' Shimon: it may even be slaughtered on account of that blemish
R' Yehuda: even if it dies, one does not let its blood
as the dispute here [over bloodletting the firstborn], so the dispute over the barrel of teruma
R' Eliezer: a barrel of teruma that came into doubtful impurity -- if in an exposed place he moves it to a concealed one, if uncovered he covers it
R' Yehoshua: if in a concealed place he may move it to an exposed one, if covered he may uncover it
Rabban Gamliel: he does nothing new with it
R' Meir [no bloodletting where it blemishes] holds like R' Eliezer [guard the barrel]
the baraita's Chachamim [bloodletting even where it blemishes] hold like R' Yehoshua [expose the barrel]
R' Yehuda [no bloodletting at all] holds like Rabban Gamliel [do nothing new]
all agree that one who leavens [a meal-offering] after another has leavened it is liable
as it is written 'it shall not be baked leavened' (Lev 6:10) and 'shall not be made leavened' (Lev 2:11)
[all agree] that one who castrates after another has castrated is liable
from 'bruised, crushed, detached or cut' (Lev 22:24): the word 'detached' is needed for nothing else, so it includes one who detaches after another has cut -- he is liable
they [the bloodletting tannaim] disputed only one who inflicts a blemish on an already-blemished animal
R' Meir holds from 'there shall be no blemish at all in it' (Lev 22:21): one may not blemish even a blemished animal
Rabbanan hold from 'perfect shall it be to be accepted' (Lev 22:21): the ban applies to a perfect animal
(first answer, abandoned) for R' Meir, 'perfect shall it be' excludes an animal blemished from the outset

rather, for R' Meir it excludes disqualified consecrated animals after their redemption -- one would think that since they remain forbidden for shearing and labour they are forbidden to blemish too; it teaches otherwise
for Rabbanan, 'any blemish' comes to forbid causing a blemish indirectly
the baraita: 'a blemish' forbids inflicting one; whence that one may not put figs or dough on the ear for a dog to come and eat? 'any blemish' -- direct and indirect alike
Shmuel / Reish Lakish / Rabba bar Avuh: 'and I, behold, I have given you the charge of My terumot' (Num 18:8) -- the verse the teruma dispute turns on
(abandoned) R' Eliezer holds the verse speaks of two terumot, pure and in abeyance, and the Merciful One said: guard it
(abandoned) R' Yehoshua: 'My teruma' (singular) is written
R' Akiva: 'bevigdo bah' -- once [the master] spread his garment over her, [the father] may no longer sell her
R' Eliezer: once [the father] dealt deceitfully with her, he may no longer sell her -- reading the written form
rather, the teruma tannaim dispute whether teruma in doubtful impurity counts as fit for you
R' Yehoshua: guard what is fit for you; what is not fit for you, do not guard
R' Eliezer: this too is fit, for perhaps Elijah will come and declare it pure
Shmuel: the halakha follows R' Shimon (which R' Shimon is the question that follows; content left unspecified)
(entertained) Shmuel means the R' Shimon of the mishna (33b.5): one may let blood even if it blemishes
(inside the hypothesis) then Shmuel would only be repeating what he has already taught: an unintended act is permitted
Rav: the halakha follows R' Yehuda [an unintended act is forbidden]
Shmuel: the halakha follows R' Shimon [an unintended act is permitted]
Shmuel's ruling follows the R' Shimon of the baraita (33b.7): the firstborn may even be slaughtered on account of the bloodletting blemish

schemas.gloss_en: if one is liable for cutting, for detaching is he not all the more so? -- so the verse's 'detached' is free to include detaching after cutting

supports.gloss_en: דתניא: מנין שלא יביא דבילה ובצק ויניחנה על האוזן... תלמוד לומר כל מום (kind tanya_kevatei for דתניא, under protest)

objections.gloss_en: ממאי? perhaps R' Meir forbids only where one blemishes by direct action, but in the barrel case, where impurity comes by grama, holds like R' Yehoshua; and R' Eliezer guards the barrel only because perhaps Elijah will purify it, but where the firstborn would certainly die if left he holds like the Rabbanan (33b.11-12)
perhaps the Rabbanan permit only here, where if left it dies; but there, perhaps Elijah will purify it -- they hold like R' Eliezer

perhaps R' Yehuda forbids only here, where one acts directly; there, by grama, he holds like R' Yehoshua; and Rabban Gamliel says do nothing only because perhaps Elijah will purify it, but here, where if left it dies, he holds like the Rabbanan (33b.13-14)
ועוד, הכא בקראי פליגי והכא בקראי פליגי -- the bloodletting tannaim dispute over Lev 22:21 (R' Yochanan, 33b.15-17) and the teruma tannaim over Num 18:8 (34a.2-6); the two disputes are not one
and R' Meir -- what does he do with 'perfect shall it be to be accepted'?

answered_by.gloss_en: it excludes disqualified consecrated animals after redemption (= p_tamim_psulei_hamukdashin); the first answer, a born-blemished animal (33b.18), fell to פשיטא, דיקלא בעלמא הוא (33b.19)

objections.gloss_en: and the Rabbanan too -- is it not written 'no blemish at all shall be in it'? (a bare verse; kind svara for want of a verse-objection kind)

answered_by.gloss_en: לגרמא הוא דאתי -- it comes to forbid causing a blemish indirectly (= p_kol_mum_lgrama)

objections.gloss_en: is R' Eliezer then of the view that the read form governs (reading תרומתי as plural)? but in the baraita on בבגדו בה he reads the written form (בגד) -- unanswered; the 34a.3 account is abandoned at 34a.6
